correctness.rationale: The graph is specified by oriented edges of K4 and has 12 vertices/18 edges. Two disjoint complete counting algorithms produce identical full densities over all 531441 spin states, recovering 91 (M,Q) sectors. Each of 74 excluded sectors has an exact rational convex domination certificate and all 17 remaining sector phases have strict rational parameter witnesses. This proves the 17-affine-function minimum for every real h/J,D/J, not just sampled fields. At h/J=D/J=1, exact full-density counting yields degeneracy 1577; at h=D=0 degeneracy 24. All certificates and counts are replayed with packaged Python 3 standard-library code.

originality.rationale: The examined same-graph Heisenberg paper has no vacancy or crystal field and cannot imply the 17-sector discrete Blume–Capel envelope. The indexed triangular-lattice Blume–Capel source has different geometry and ferromagnetic thermal behavior. The identically titled truncated tetrahedral model places twelve directional states at each square-lattice site, not spins on the truncated tetrahedron. Prior accessible same-graph Potts ground states penalize equal zero-color neighbors whereas the present zero spin decouples; other spin-one clusters use different graphs. No matching or stronger exact two-parameter spin-one table was found in actual indexed/primary comparisons, but unindexed tables remain a historical risk.
residual_risks: Searchable published research is incomplete; historical spin-one ground-state tables for the truncated-tetrahedral cluster might use an alternate naming convention.
Thermodynamic phase diagram papers for other finite clusters do not give a general priority guarantee.
The same-model proof and computation checks are not an external independent audit.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated 12-site fullerene-proxy geometry has triangle frustration, and the spin-one Blume–Capel Hamiltonian adds physically motivated vacancy/anisotropy control. The exact complete two-parameter phase diagram has 17 genuinely open magnetization/occupancy phases and a nontrivial 1577-fold coexistence point, including vacancy-driven sectors absent on the zero-anisotropy line. A complete finite-cluster benchmark supplies more information than a routine field sample or color relabeling; no thermodynamic extrapolation is asserted.
